changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: For ticketing and live-event buyers: "A name, not a queue. Your named team is on the line during your biggest moments: someone who picks up." Lead with the named people and the event-coverage commitment, not tiers or response timers. Keep the word "support" out of the headline.
changes.why: The decider dismissed our tiered plans as "a queue with a faster timer" after the competitor put named people in the room and promised on-sale on-call, and the customer's own words were "a name, not a queue" and "someone who picks up."

changes.change: New proof point for ticketing and event buyers, written for the COO or ops owner: "Your on-sale morning plan, on paper: who's watching, who you call, and what happens at minute four." Back it with a documented peak-event plan that the SE can tailor to each customer's on-sale calendar.
changes.why: The COO asked to see on paper what we do on an on-sale morning, including who's watching, who she calls and what happens at minute four, and we had nothing packaged. The trigger was payments failing four minutes in with no reply until the on-sale was over.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: For high-stakes-event buyers, replace logo proof with a person: "Talk to [ticketing customer] about who picked up during their biggest on-sale." This requires recruiting a ticketing or event reference who can speak to a live incident.
changes.why: The rep said "I had logos. I didn't have a person," and logos did not answer the decider's question of who handles a live on-sale.

changes.current_line: Built for developers: launch payments fast with our APIs, docs and sandbox.
changes.change: In ticketing and event deals where ops or the COO owns the decision, stop leading with developer, sandbox and uptime proof. Keep it as the CTO-track technical proof. Open the COO conversation with: "You don't buy uptime, you buy what happens when it's down."
changes.why: The sandbox load test won over Ben, the CTO, who didn't decide. Halima, who made the call in one meeting, gave it a one-word "good." and said "I don't buy uptime, I buy what happens when it's down."
